body: We investigate associative creativity in descriptions of abstract visual stimuli by humans and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While conceptual association is central to human communication, it remains unclear how humans and models adapt when visual stimuli become increasingly difficult to map onto familiar semantic concepts. We evaluate several state-of-the-art MLLMs and human participants along two dimensions of creativity, originality and effectiveness, using two datasets with controlled manipulations of difficulty. SilCC varies naming difficulty through progressively more complex combinations of abstract shapes, and PixCC varies difficulty through increasing levels of random visual noise. Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica. As difficulty increases, effectiveness declines in SilCC, and humans increasingly shift from holistic associations to descriptions of low-level visual properties in PixCC.
summaryZh: 用难以命名的视觉刺激测试人类和多模态法学硕士的联想创造力。我们研究人类和多模态大语言模型（MLLM）对抽象视觉刺激的描述中的联想创造力。虽然概念关联是人类交流的核心，但当视觉刺激变得越来越难以映射到熟悉的语义概念时，人类和模型如何适应仍不清楚。
